mainTopic: God's goodness, whether He rejoices when רשעים fall, and stories of אחאב, עובדיהו and מואב that close the פרק
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that the Jewish people are not counted among 'the nations.' רבי אלעזר then resolves two פסוקים about whom ה׳ is good to with a parable of an orchard: watering reaches every tree, but hoeing is only for the good ones. Returning to the משנה's 'באבוד רשעים רנה,' the גמרא connects it to the song at אחאב's death. It then asks whether הקדוש ברוך הוא rejoices when רשעים fall. רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers that He does not rejoice Himself, but He causes others to rejoice. More teachings follow about אחאב's death, which fulfilled the prophecies of מיכיהו and אליהו. Next comes praise of עובדיהו: he feared ה׳ greatly, he hid a hundred prophets, and he prophesied against אדום, perhaps as an Edomite convert ('the ax comes from the forest itself'). The amud then discusses the king of מואב who sacrificed his son, and ends the פרק by comparing אבישג's beauty to שרה's.

steps.title: The Jewish people are not counted among 'the nations'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a proof from the previous discussion. It quotes a פסוק showing that the Jewish people are not included in the word 'nations'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And shall not be reckoned among the nations.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier proof by quoting the end of a פסוק. It shows that the Jewish people are a separate group and are not counted with 'the nations'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא was discussing how to read the word 'nations' in a פסוק. This פסוק from בלעם's blessing settles it: Israel 'shall not be reckoned among the nations.' So when a פסוק says 'nations', it does not include ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Will not be counted or reckoned

phrases.english: "And shall not be reckoned among the nations."
phrases.notes: במדבר 23:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a proof that began before this section
steps.raayaObject: The Jewish people are not included in the word 'nations'

steps.title: Two verses about whom God is good to
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר points out that one פסוק says ה׳ is good to everyone, while another says He is good to those who hope in Him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר points out a contradiction. One פסוק says, 'ה׳ is good to all.' Another פסוק says, 'ה׳ is good to those who hope in Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר places two פסוקים side by side that seem to disagree. This sets up his answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק (תהלים) says God's goodness reaches everyone. The second פסוק (איכה) seems to limit it to people who hope in Him. Both cannot be fully true unless they describe two different kinds of goodness.

keyTerms.meaning: He points out a contradiction (literally, 'he throws' two sources against each other)
To those who hope in Him

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar raises a contradiction:
It is written, "The Lord is good to all,"
phrases.notes: תהלים 145:9

phrases.english: and it is written, "The Lord is good to those who hope in Him."
phrases.notes: איכה 3:25

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected by theme: how God relates to everyone versus to the righteous
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים: 'טוב ה׳ לכל' and 'טוב ה׳ לקויו'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק makes God's goodness universal, while the other seems to limit it to those who hope in Him.

steps.title: The orchard parable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר compares this to an orchard owner. When he waters, all the trees get water. When he hoes, he works only around the good trees.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a man who owns an orchard. When he waters it, he waters all of it. When he hoes, he hoes only around the good trees.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the contradiction with a parable. Each פסוק describes a different kind of goodness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Watering is general: the water spreads to every tree, so it matches 'טוב ה׳ לכל'. Hoeing is special care given tree by tree, so it matches 'טוב ה׳ לקויו'. God gives general goodness to everyone, but gives extra, personal care to those who hope in Him.

keyTerms.meaning: Hoes (loosens the soil around a plant)

steps.whatToRemember: God's goodness comes on two levels: general goodness for all, like watering a whole orchard, and special care for the righteous, like hoeing around the good trees.

phrases.english: It is comparable to a person
who has an orchard:
when he waters, he waters all of it;
when he hoes,
phrases.notes: Hoeing means digging around one tree at a time to help it grow. It is personal care, not general care.

phrases.english: he hoes only the good ones among them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רבי אלעזר's contradiction
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק describes a different kind of goodness
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to give opposite answers about who receives God's goodness
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לכל' means general goodness for everyone; 'לקויו' means special care for those who hope in Him

steps.title: Back to the משנה: 'Therefore each and every one'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the line of the משנה that begins 'לפיכך כל אחד ואחד', which goes on to quote 'באבוד רשעים רנה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Therefore each and every one,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the משנה again to set up its next discussion. The discussion is about the פסוק 'באבוד רשעים רנה', which the משנה quotes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה tells the witnesses that they should not hold back testimony because they fear being responsible for a person's death, since 'when the wicked perish, there is song.' The גמרא now wants to explain that פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for 'and so on'; the rest of the line is assumed

phrases.english: Therefore, each and every one, etc.
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the משנה, which goes on to quote 'באבוד רשעים רנה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side topic and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes the משנה as the topic for the next discussion

steps.title: The 'song' when אחאב died
steps.stepSummary: רבי אחא בר חנינא links 'באבוד רשעים רנה' to the song that went through the camp when אחאב בן עמרי died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'And the song went through the camp.' רבי אחא בר חנינא says: 'When the wicked perish, there is song' refers to this. When אחאב son of עמרי died, there was song.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אחא בר חנינא explains that the 'song' in the camp after אחאב's death is the song meant in the פסוק 'באבוד רשעים רנה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in מלכים says 'the song,' as if it means a song we already know about. רבי אחא בר חנינא identifies it with the 'רנה' of משלי. This makes it sound as if the downfall of the wicked is a reason for joyful song.
steps.confusionAlert: The song described here is people singing, not God rejoicing. The next step asks exactly whether God shares this joy.

phrases.english: "And the song passed through the camp."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 22:36, right after אחאב is killed in battle.

phrases.english: Rabbi Acha bar Chanina says:
"When the wicked perish, there is song"
phrases.notes: משלי 11:10

phrases.english: means: when Ahab son of Omri perished, there was song.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'באבוד רשעים רנה' refers to the song in the camp when אחאב died

steps.title: Does God rejoice when the wicked fall?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether הקדוש ברוך הוא really rejoices when רשעים fall. It quotes a פסוק about a victory song that leaves out the words 'כי טוב'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does הקדוש ברוך הוא rejoice when the wicked fall? Isn't it written: 'As they went out before the army, they said: Give thanks to ה׳, for His kindness lasts forever'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the fall of the wicked brings joy. It begins by quoting a victory song from דברי הימים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 suggested that the downfall of רשעים calls for song. The גמרא doubts that God Himself rejoices at it. It brings a victory song in which something seems to be missing; the next step explains what is missing.

phrases.english: But does the Holy One, Blessed be He, rejoice
at the downfall of the wicked?
But isn't it written:
"As they went out before the army,
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 20:21

phrases.aramaic: וְאֹמְרִים הוֹדוּ לַה׳ כִּי לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ״.
phrases.english: and said: Give thanks to the Lord, for His kindness is forever."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי חָדֵי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בְּמַפַּלְתָּן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the implication of רבי אחא בר חנינא's teaching
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the fall of רשעים is a cause for joy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A victory song over enemies seems to hold back full praise, which suggests that God does not rejoice when the wicked fall.

steps.title: רבי יונתן: why 'כי טוב' is missing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן explains that the words 'כי טוב' were left out of this praise because הקדוש ברוך הוא is not happy when רשעים fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יונתן said: Why does this praise not say 'for He is good'? Because הקדוש ברוך הוא is not happy when the wicked fall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes its challenge with רבי יונתן's teaching. This is the proof that God does not rejoice at the downfall of the wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual form of this praise is 'הודו לה׳ כי טוב כי לעולם חסדו'. In this battle song, 'כי טוב' is missing. רבי יונתן says it was left out on purpose because God takes no joy in the death of רשעים, even enemies. This seems to contradict the 'רנה' at אחאב's death; step 9 answers this.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יונתן, God is not happy at the downfall of the wicked. That is why 'כי טוב' is left out of the victory praise.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the tension the גמרא must resolve next: how can there be 'רנה' when רשעים perish if God Himself does not rejoice?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yonatan said:
For what reason is it not said
in this praise, "for He is good"?
phrases.notes: The usual wording is 'הודו לה׳ כי טוב כי לעולם חסדו', as in תהלים 118:1.

phrases.english: Because the Holy One, Blessed be He, is not
happy at the downfall of the wicked.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא נֶאֱמַר בְּהוֹדָאָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge by explaining why the quoted פסוק is a problem
steps.raayaObject: הקדוש ברוך הוא does not rejoice at the downfall of רשעים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'כי טוב' are missing from the praise in דברי הימים ב 20:21, as explained by רבי יונתן

steps.title: The angels were not allowed to sing at the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן teaches that when the מצרים drowned, the מלאכי השרת wanted to sing. הקדוש ברוך הוא stopped them, because His creations were dying.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי שמואל בר נחמן said in the name of רבי יונתן: What does the פסוק mean, 'And the one did not come near the other all the night'? At that time the ministering angels wanted to sing before הקדוש ברוך הוא. He said to them: My handiwork is drowning in the sea, and you want to sing before Me?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source that backs up the previous step: הקדוש ברוך הוא is not happy when רשעים fall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, רבי יונתן explained that 'כי טוב' was left out of the praise because הקדוש ברוך הוא does not rejoice when רשעים fall. Here he brings a story to prove it. Even the מצרים are called 'My handiwork', and the angels were not allowed to sing while they drowned.

keyTerms.meaning: My handiwork, meaning the people I created

steps.confusionAlert: Only the angels were stopped from singing. The גמרא does not say that בני ישראל were wrong to sing אז ישיר.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachman said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
What is the meaning of that which is written

phrases.aramaic: ״וְלֹא קָרַב זֶה אֶל זֶה כׇּל הַלָּיְלָה״?
phrases.english: "And the one did not come near the other all the night"?
phrases.notes: שמות 14:20

phrases.english: At that time
the ministering angels wanted

phrases.aramaic: לוֹמַר שִׁירָה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא.
phrases.english: to say a song before the Holy One, Blessed be He.
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:
My handiwork is drowning in the sea,
phrases.notes: He means the Egyptians, who were drowning in ים סוף.

phrases.english: and you are saying a song before Me?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind רבי יונתן's claim in step 7 that הקדוש ברוך הוא does not rejoice when רשעים fall.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that הקדוש ברוך הוא is not happy when רשעים fall
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יונתן's teaching about the angels at ים סוף, based on 'ולא קרב זה אל זה כל הלילה'

steps.title: He does not rejoice, but He makes others rejoice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר חנינא settles the problem. הקדוש ברוך הוא Himself does not rejoice when רשעים fall, but He causes others to rejoice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: He Himself does not rejoice, but He makes others rejoice.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר חנינא answers the question from step 6 by splitting it into two parts: what הקדוש ברוך הוא feels, and what He causes others to feel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that 'באבוד רשעים רנה' sounds like there is joy, while רבי יונתן showed that הקדוש ברוך הוא is not happy. The answer is that both are true. He is not happy, but He lets people rejoice when רשעים are gone.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how the משנה can quote 'באבוד רשעים רנה' even though הקדוש ברוך הוא does not rejoice at the fall of the wicked.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
He does not rejoice,
phrases.notes: "He" means הקדוש ברוך הוא.

phrases.english: but He makes others rejoice.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא: הוּא אֵינוֹ שָׂשׂ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the conflict between 'באבוד רשעים רנה' and the proofs that הקדוש ברוך הוא does not rejoice.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: הקדוש ברוך הוא's own feeling versus the joy He causes in others
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that there is either joy at the fall of רשעים or there is not, so the sources clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: הקדוש ברוך הוא does not rejoice, but He causes others to rejoice, so 'באבוד רשעים רנה' is about people's joy.

steps.title: The exact word 'ישיש' proves it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the wording of a פסוק fits רבי יוסי בר חנינא. The פסוק says 'ישיש' (He will cause joy), not 'ישוש' (He will be joyful).
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise: it is written 'ישיש' (He will cause rejoicing), and it is not written 'ישוש' (He will rejoice). Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי יוסי בר חנינא from the exact spelling of a word in a פסוק, and then accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים talks about הקדוש ברוך הוא bringing destruction on sinners. If it meant He Himself rejoices, it would say 'ישוש'. Instead it says 'ישיש', a form that means making others rejoice, just as רבי יוסי בר חנינא said.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact, so it supports this
He will cause others to rejoice
Learn from it, the proof is accepted

steps.whatToRemember: הקדוש ברוך הוא does not rejoice when רשעים fall, but He causes others to rejoice. The word 'ישיש' instead of 'ישוש' shows this.

phrases.english: The wording is also precise,
as it is written "yasis" (He will cause rejoicing)
phrases.notes: דברים 28:63

phrases.english: and it is not written "yasus" (He will rejoice).
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוסי בר חנינא's answer from the exact wording of a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי בר חנינא's teaching that He makes others rejoice
steps.raayaSupportSource: The form 'ישיש' rather than 'ישוש' in דברים 28:63

steps.title: The 'harlots' are two prophecies coming true
steps.stepSummary: Back to the death of אחאב: רבי אלעזר reads 'והזונות רחצו' as 'visions'. אחאב's death fulfilled two prophecies, one by מיכיהו and one by אליהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the harlots washed, etc.' רבי אלעזר said: This means to fully carry out two visions, one of מיכיהו and one of אליהו. About מיכיהו it is written: 'If you return at all in peace, the Lord has not spoken through me.' About אליהו it is written: 'In the place where the dogs licked the blood of נבות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of אחאב's death and explains a strange phrase in that פסוק, 'and the harlots washed'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר reads 'זונות' as if it said 'חזיונות', prophetic visions. אחאב died in battle, so מיכיהו's warning that he would not come back in peace came true. The dogs licked his blood, so אליהו's prophecy came true too.

keyTerms.meaning: To cleanse, here meaning to fulfill completely
And so on, the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: "And the harlots washed, etc."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 22:38, describing the washing of אחאב's chariot after he died.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
To cleanse two visions,
phrases.notes: He reads זונות (harlots) as חזיונות (visions). "Cleanse" here means to fulfill them completely.

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל מִיכָיְהוּ וְאַחַת שֶׁל אֵלִיָּהוּ.
phrases.english: one of Michayhu and one of Eliyahu.
About Michayhu it is written:
"If you return at all in peace,
the Lord has not spoken through me";
phrases.notes: מלכים א 22:28

phrases.english: About Eliyahu it is written:
"In the place where the dogs licked
the blood of Navot."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 21:19. The פסוק goes on to say the dogs will lick אחאב's blood there too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question about joy and returns to the story of אחאב's death from step 5, explaining another phrase in that passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'הזונות' hints at 'חזיונות': אחאב's death fulfilled the prophecies of מיכיהו and אליהו.

steps.title: רבא: they were real images of harlots
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees and reads the word plainly. איזבל had pictures of זונות made on אחאב's chariot to arouse him, and these were washed along with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: They were actual harlots. אחאב was a cold man, so איזבל made him two images of harlots on his chariot, so that he would see them and become aroused.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second explanation of 'והזונות רחצו' that reads the word in its simple meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר read the word as 'visions', but רבא says it really means harlots. They were pictures that איזבל put on אחאב's chariot, because he had little desire. When the chariot was washed, these images were washed too.

phrases.english: Rava said: They were actual harlots.
Achav was a cold man,
phrases.notes: He means אחאב had little desire for women.

phrases.english: and Izevel made for him
two images of harlots in his chariot,
so that he would see them and become aroused.
phrases.notes: So in the פסוק, it was these images that got washed along with the chariot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different, plain reading of the same phrase that רבי אלעזר explained in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'הזונות' means actual images of harlots that איזבל placed on אחאב's chariot.

steps.title: The archer shot without aiming
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says a man drew his bow 'לתמו' and struck אחאב. רבי אלעזר explains that this means he shot innocently, without aiming at the king.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And a man drew his bow לתמו and struck the king.' רבי אלעזר says this means 'in his innocence.' The archer was not trying to hit אחאב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק describing the arrow that killed אחאב. רבי אלעזר explains the unusual word 'לתמו' in a simple way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, the word 'לתמו' tells us the archer shot randomly, with no plan to kill the king. He reads the word as describing the archer's state of mind, while רבא in the next step reads it as describing what the arrow achieved.

keyTerms.meaning: A bow, used for shooting arrows
An unusual word in the פסוק, explained in two ways in this step and the next

phrases.english: "And a man drew his bow
phrases.notes: מלכים א 22:34

phrases.english: letumo, and struck" the king of Israel.
Rabbi Elazar says:
In his innocence, without aiming.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of אחאב's death from steps 11 and 12 with another פסוק from the same story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לתמו' means the archer shot innocently, without aiming at אחאב.

steps.title: The arrow completed two prophecies
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads 'לתמו' as 'to complete.' The arrow completed two prophecies about אחאב, one from מיכיהו and one from אליהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: 'לתמו' means 'to complete.' The arrow completed two visions, one of מיכיהו and one of אליהו.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different reading of the same word. He connects 'לתמו' to the word for completing something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר explained the word as describing the archer's mindset. רבא explains it as describing the result: this one arrow fulfilled two separate prophecies at once. This fits the earlier point from step 11 that אחאב's death fulfilled the words of both מיכיהו and אליהו.

keyTerms.meaning: The נביא who foretold that אחאב would fall in battle
The נביא who foretold that dogs would lick אחאב's blood

steps.whatToRemember: The single arrow that killed אחאב fulfilled two prophecies at the same moment, one by מיכיהו and one by אליהו.

phrases.english: Rava says:
To complete two visions,
one of Michayhu
and one of Eliyahu.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second reading of the same word that רבי אלעזר explained in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'לתמו' means 'to complete': the arrow fulfilled the prophecies of both מיכיהו and אליהו.

steps.title: Why does the verse mention עובדיהו's fear of ה׳?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a memory aid for the coming teachings. Then it quotes the פסוק about אחאב calling עובדיהו and asks what the פסוק is trying to tell us.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory aid: called, merited, of Edom.) It is written: 'And אחאב called עובדיהו, who was over the household, and עובדיהו feared ה׳ greatly.' What is the פסוק saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic about עובדיהו. It asks why the פסוק adds his fear of ה׳ right after saying that אחאב called him. This sets up רבי יצחק's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to jump from one thing to another. First it says אחאב called his household manager, then it suddenly praises that manager's fear of ה׳. The גמרא wants to know how these two parts connect.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid listing key words of the coming teachings
The manager of אחאב's household, who feared ה׳
Who was in charge of the household

phrases.english: (A memory aid: Called; and merited; of Edom.)
It is written: "And Achav called Ovadyahu,
who was over the household,
and Ovadyahu feared ה׳ greatly."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:3. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: What is the verse saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from אחאב's death to a new topic within the stories of אחאב: his servant עובדיהו.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What connects אחאב calling עובדיהו with the statement that עובדיהו feared ה׳ greatly?

steps.title: אחאב blames עובדיהו, and a בת קול answers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that אחאב complained to עובדיהו. When יעקב and יוסף ran other people's houses, those houses were blessed, but אחאב's house was not, so maybe עובדיהו did not fear ה׳. A בת קול answered that עובדיהו did fear ה׳ greatly. The problem was that אחאב's house was not fit for blessing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: אחאב said to עובדיהו, 'About יעקב it is written, "ה׳ blessed me because of you." About יוסף it is written, "ה׳ blessed the Egyptian's house because of יוסף." My house has not been blessed. Maybe you do not fear ה׳?' A בת קול came out and said, 'עובדיהו feared ה׳ greatly,' but the house of אחאב is not fit for blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers the question by filling in a conversation. אחאב called עובדיהו to accuse him, and the second half of the פסוק is Heaven's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחאב reasoned from earlier examples: a righteous manager brings blessing to the house he runs, as with לבן and פוטיפר. Since his own house was not blessed, he concluded that עובדיהו must not be righteous. The בת קול turns the blame back on אחאב: עובדיהו was truly righteous, but אחאב's wicked house blocked the blessing.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of you, for your sake
'That man,' a polite way of saying 'me'
Fit or ready to receive blessing

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read the בת קול as saying that עובדיהו failed. It defends him completely. The lack of blessing came from אחאב's house, not from עובדיהו.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: He said to him,
phrases.notes: אחאב is speaking to עובדיהו.

phrases.english: About Yaakov it is written:
"I have seen the signs, and ה׳ blessed me because of you,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 30:27. These are לבן's words to יעקב.

phrases.english: About Yosef it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיְבָרֶךְ ה׳ אֶת בֵּית הַמִּצְרִי בִּגְלַל יוֹסֵף״.
phrases.english: "And ה׳ blessed the Egyptian's house because of Yosef."
phrases.notes: בראשית 39:5

phrases.english: The house of that man
phrases.notes: אחאב means his own house. 'That man' is a polite way to avoid saying 'me' in something negative.

phrases.english: was not blessed.
Perhaps you do not fear God?
A Heavenly voice came out and said:
"And Ovadyahu feared ה׳ greatly,"
but the house of Achav
is not fit for blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 15 by explaining how the two halves of the פסוק connect.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחאב called עובדיהו to accuse him of not fearing ה׳, since his house was not blessed. The second half of the פסוק is a בת קול answering that עובדיהו feared ה׳ greatly, and that אחאב's house was the reason there was no blessing.

steps.title: עובדיהו is praised more than אברהם
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא points out that the פסוק praises עובדיהו with the word 'מאד' (greatly). This word does not appear in the praise of אברהם's fear of God.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: What is said about עובדיהו is greater than what is said about אברהם. About אברהם, 'greatly' is not written, but about עובדיהו, 'greatly' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא adds a further point about the same פסוק. He compares the praise of עובדיהו to the praise of אברהם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both אברהם and עובדיהו are described as fearing God. Only עובדיהו's description includes the extra word 'מאד.' רבי אבא learns from this extra word that the praise given to עובדיהו is greater.
steps.whatToRemember: The single word 'מאד' in the פסוק gives עובדיהו a level of praise for fearing ה׳ that is not written even about אברהם.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
Greater is what is said about Ovadyahu
than what is said about Avraham,
for about Avraham "greatly" is not written,
phrases.notes: The פסוק about אברהם is בראשית 22:12, 'for now I know that you fear God.'

phrases.english: but about Ovadyahu "greatly" is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: גָּדוֹל שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּעוֹבַדְיָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the same פסוק about עובדיהו, now focusing on the word 'מאד.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because 'מאד' is written about עובדיהו but not about אברהם, the praise of עובדיהו's fear of ה׳ is greater.

steps.title: Why עובדיהו became a prophet
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says עובדיהו merited prophecy because he hid one hundred prophets in a cave, and he brings the פסוק that shows this.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Why did עובדיהו merit prophecy? Because he hid one hundred prophets in a cave, as the פסוק says: 'When איזבל was killing the prophets of ה׳, עובדיהו took one hundred prophets and hid them, fifty men in a cave.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives the reason עובדיהו was rewarded with נבואה: he risked his life to hide one hundred prophets from איזבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the earlier praise of עובדיהו's fear of ה׳ (Steps 16-17). Now we learn a concrete act that earned him נבואה. The פסוק's detail of 'fifty men in a cave' sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: when [she] was cutting off, wiping out

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
For what reason did Obadiah merit prophecy?
Because he hid one hundred prophets in a cave,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיְהִי בְּהַכְרִית אִיזֶבֶל אֵת נְבִיאֵי ה׳
phrases.english: as it says: “And it was, when Jezebel was cutting off the prophets of God,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 18:4

phrases.english: Obadiah took one hundred prophets
and hid them, fifty men to a cave, etc.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: מִפְּנֵי מָה זָכָה עוֹבַדְיָהוּ לִנְבִיאוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues praising עובדיהו after רבי אבא's teaching about the word 'מאד'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עובדיהו merited נבואה because he hid one hundred prophets from איזבל.

steps.title: Why groups of fifty?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why עובדיהו split the prophets into groups of fifty.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about fifty men?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the פסוק just quoted. It is setting up two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'fifty men in a cave', which means he used two caves. The גמרא wants to know why he did not hide all one hundred together.

keyTerms.meaning: what is different, why this specifically

phrases.english: What is different about fifty men?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail in the פסוק quoted in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why עובדיהו divided the prophets into two groups of fifty.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: He learned from יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says עובדיהו learned from יעקב to split into groups, so that if one group was found, the other would survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: He learned this from יעקב, as the פסוק says: 'and the camp that is left will escape.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers that splitting the prophets was a safety plan that עובדיהו copied from יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב divided his camp in two before meeting עשו, so that if one camp was attacked the other could escape. עובדיהו did the same: if איזבל found one cave, the prophets in the other cave would live.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
He learned it from Jacob,
as it says: “And the camp that is left shall escape.”
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:9. יעקב split his people into two camps before meeting עשו.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He split them so that if one group was caught, the other would survive. He learned this from יעקב.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: A cave only holds fifty
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו gives a practical answer: no cave could hold more than fifty people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: Because a cave cannot hold more than fifty people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו offers a second answer to the same question. His answer is simply about space.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר saw a planned safety strategy. רבי אבהו gives a simple practical reason instead: a cave could not fit more than fifty, so he had to use two caves.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מְעָרָה מַחְזֶקֶת יוֹתֵר מֵחֲמִשִּׁים.
phrases.english: Because no cave holds more than fifty.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מְעָרָה מַחְזֶקֶת יוֹתֵר מֵחֲמִשִּׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, practical answer to Step 19's question, different from רבי אלעזר's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Groups of fifty were needed because a cave holds no more than fifty.

steps.title: Why did עובדיהו prophesy about אדום?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening of ספר עובדיה, which is about אדום, and asks why עובדיהו in particular was sent with this prophecy.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'The vision of עובדיהו: So says ה׳ אלהים about אדום.' Why was עובדיהו the one to prophesy about אדום?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question about עובדיהו. It is setting up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ספר עובדיה is a prophecy against אדום, the nation that came from עשו. The גמרא wants to know what link there is between this prophet and this nation.

keyTerms.meaning: Edom, the nation that came from עשו

phrases.english: “The vision of Obadiah:
phrases.notes: עובדיה 1:1

phrases.aramaic: כֹּה אָמַר ה׳ אֱלֹהִים לֶאֱדוֹם וְגוֹ׳״.
phrases.english: So says God concerning Edom, etc.”
What is different about Obadiah, that he prophesied about Edom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Still about עובדיהו, but asks a new question about his prophecy.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why עובדיהו specifically was chosen to prophesy about אדום.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: The perfect contrast to עשו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says ה׳ chose עובדיהו because he stayed righteous while living among two wicked people. That made him the right one to judge עשו, who stayed wicked while living among two righteous people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: הקדוש ברוך הוא said, 'Let עובדיהו come, who lives between two wicked people and did not learn from their deeds, and let him prophesy against the wicked עשו, who lived between two righteous people and did not learn from their deeds.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains that עובדיהו's life is a mirror opposite of עשו's life, and that is why he was sent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עובדיהו lived in the house of אחאב and איזבל but stayed righteous. עשו grew up with יצחק and רבקה but stayed wicked. עובדיהו's life shows that עשו had no excuse.

keyTerms.meaning: the Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:

phrases.aramaic: יָבֹא עוֹבַדְיָהוּ הַדָּר בֵּין שְׁנֵי רְשָׁעִים
phrases.english: Let Obadiah come, who lives between two wicked people,
phrases.notes: These are אחאב and איזבל, whose house עובדיהו ran.

phrases.english: and did not learn from their deeds,
and let him prophesy about the wicked Esau,
who lived between two righteous people,
phrases.notes: These are his parents, יצחק and רבקה.

phrases.english: and did not learn from their deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, יָבֹא עוֹבַדְיָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 22's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עובדיהו's righteousness among the wicked condemns עשו's wickedness among the righteous.

steps.title: עובדיהו was an Edomite convert
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רבי מאיר, his student אפרים מקשאה says עובדיהו was a convert from אדום. This fits the saying that the ax that chops the forest has a handle made from the forest's own wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: אפרים מקשאה, the student of רבי מאיר, said in the name of רבי מאיר: עובדיהו was an Edomite convert. This is what people say: 'From the forest itself comes the ax that cuts it.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a second answer to why עובדיהו prophesied about אדום: he came from אדום himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק's answer was about contrast. This answer is about where עובדיהו came from: one of אדום's own people was sent to announce its downfall. The folk saying captures this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: as people say (introduces a folk saying)

phrases.english: Efrayim Miksha'a,

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: the student of Rabbi Meir, said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
Obadiah was an Edomite convert.
And this is what people say:
From it and within it, the forest,
the ax goes into it.
phrases.notes: The ax's wooden handle comes from the very forest it chops down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אֶפְרַיִם מִקְשָׁאָה תַּלְמִידוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי מֵאִיר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reason for Step 22's question, based on עובדיהו's origin.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עובדיהו came from אדום, so one of its own people announced its punishment.
steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons why עובדיהו prophesied about אדום: (1) his righteous life is the opposite of עשו's, and (2) he himself came from אדום, like an ax handle made from the forest's own wood.

steps.title: The same saying applied to דוד and מואב
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says דוד struck מואב. רבי יוחנן, in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי, applies the same 'ax from the forest' saying here.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'He struck מואב and measured them with a rope, making them lie on the ground.' רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: This is what people say: 'From the forest itself comes the ax that cuts it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second example of the same idea: מואב was punished by דוד, who came from מואב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד came from רות, a convert from מואב. So מואב was defeated by one of its own descendants, just like the ax handle from the forest.

keyTerms.meaning: Moab, a nation near ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: “And he struck Moab
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 8:2. This is about דוד.

phrases.english: and measured them with the rope,
making them lie down on the ground.”

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
This is what people say:
From it and within it, the forest,
the ax goes into it.
phrases.notes: דוד came from רות the Moabite, so מואב was struck by one of its own descendants.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same folk saying from Step 24 to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דוד, a descendant of מואב, defeating מואב fits the saying that the ax comes from the forest itself.

steps.title: רב דימי: A thigh rots from within
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי, arriving from ארץ ישראל, gives a similar saying: a thigh of meat begins to rot from the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: A thigh rots from within.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי adds another folk saying with the same message: destruction comes from inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat spoils starting from its inner part. In the same way, a nation's downfall can come through someone from within it, like דוד from מואב.

keyTerms.meaning: when [he] came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
A thigh rots from within.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel saying to the one in Step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ruin begins from within, just as a thigh of meat rots from the inside.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sayings, the ax from the forest and the thigh that rots from within, teach the same idea: a nation can be brought down by one of its own.

steps.title: The king of Moab offers his son: two views on why
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק about the king of מואב offering his firstborn son on the wall. רב and שמואל disagree: one says it was for the sake of Heaven, the other says it was for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Then he took his eldest son, who would have reigned in his place, and offered him up as a burnt offering on the wall.' רב and שמואל disagree. One says he did it for the sake of Heaven, and one says he did it for idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting a פסוק about the king of מואב and brings a disagreement between רב and שמואל about his intention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king of מואב was losing a war against ישראל and offered his own son on the wall. The question is to whom the offering was made: one view says it was to ה׳, the other says it was to an idol. This disagreement sets up the next step, where the גמרא tests each view against the rest of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, a sacrifice burned completely
One says (used when two Sages disagree and the גמרא doesn't say who held which view)
For the sake of Heaven, meaning offered to ה׳

phrases.english: "Then he took his eldest son,
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 3:27. "He" is the king of מואב, who was losing a war against ישראל.

phrases.english: who would have reigned in his place,
and offered him up as a burnt offering on the wall."
Rav and Shmuel disagree:
One says: it was for the sake of Heaven,
and one says: it was for the sake of idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל, חַד אָמַר: לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, וְחַד אָמַר: לְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sayings about attackers coming from within (steps 24 through 26) to another פסוק about מואב. This one is about a different war, the one against the king of מואב told in מלכים ב 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב and שמואל disagree whether the king of מואב sacrificed his son to ה׳ or to an idol.

steps.title: Why was there anger against Israel if it was idol worship?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the 'for Heaven' view explains the anger against ישראל in the פסוק. But on the 'idol worship' view, why would ה׳ be angry at ישראל?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the one who says it was for the sake of Heaven: that is why it says 'And there was great anger against Israel.' But for the one who says it was for idol worship, why does it say 'And there was anger'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests both views against the next words of the פסוק and finds that the idol-worship view seems to have a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק continues 'there was great anger against ישראל.' If a non-Jewish king offered something to ה׳, it makes sense that ישראל would be judged harshly by comparison. But if he offered it to an idol, there seems to be no reason for ה׳ to be angry at ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well (for one view); signals a challenge to the other view is coming
According to the one who says

phrases.english: It works well for the one who says it was for the sake of Heaven:
that is why it is written:
"And there was great anger against Israel."
phrases.notes: These are the next words of the same פסוק, מלכים ב 3:27.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְשֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: But according to the one who says it was for idol worship,
why does it say "and there was anger"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one side of the disagreement brought in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the king of מואב sacrificed his son for עבודה זרה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says there was anger against ישראל. That fits only if the king did something good in comparison to ישראל, which is not the case if he served an idol.

steps.title: Israel copied the worst of the nations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers using רבי יהושע בן לוי's resolution of two contradicting פסוקים: ישראל did not copy the good nations, but did copy the corrupt ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching. He pointed out a contradiction: one פסוק says 'You have not acted like the laws of the nations around you,' and another says 'You have acted like the laws of the nations around you.' The answer: you did not act like the proper ones among them, but you did act like the corrupt ones among them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the idol-worship view by bringing רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching that ישראל imitated the corrupt practices of the nations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי settles the two פסוקים in יחזקאל by splitting the nations into good and bad: ישראל copied only the bad. Applied here, the anger is explained even if the king served an idol, because ישראל followed his corrupt example instead of the nations' good ways. So the 'anger' does not prove the king acted for Heaven.

keyTerms.meaning: Points out a contradiction between two sources
The laws or practices of the nations

phrases.english: It is in line with the teaching of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi points out a contradiction:
It is written: "And like the laws of the nations
that are around you, you have not acted,"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 5:7

phrases.english: and it is written: "And like the laws of the nations
that are around you, you have acted."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 11:12

phrases.english: Like the proper ones among them, you did not act;
like the corrupt ones among them, you did act.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי רָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28 so that the idol-worship view still stands.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an outside teaching that gives a different reason for the anger.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The anger against ישראל only makes sense if the king did something praiseworthy, meaning he served ה׳.
steps.terutzMaskana: The anger also makes sense if he served an idol, because ישראל copied the corrupt ways of the nations.
steps.whatToRemember: Both views of רב and שמואל can explain the 'anger': either the king put ישראל to shame by serving ה׳, or ישראל copied his corrupt act.

steps.title: Israel sank to the lowest level
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the פסוק, 'and they returned to the land,' and רבי חנינא בר פפא teaches that at that moment ישראל fell to the lowest level.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they departed from him and returned to the land.' רבי חנינא בר פפא says: At that time, the enemies of Israel went down to the lowest level.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the פסוק and brings רבי חנינא בר פפא's teaching about its last words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word לָאָרֶץ can mean 'to the land' but also 'to the ground.' רבי חנינא בר פפא reads it as 'down to the ground,' showing that ישראל's spiritual level dropped to its lowest point at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: To the land, or to the ground
The enemies of ישראל, a polite way of saying ישראל itself

steps.confusionAlert: 'The enemies of Israel' does not mean the actual enemies. It is a polite way the גמרא uses to avoid saying something bad directly about ישראל.

phrases.english: "And they departed from him
and returned to the land."
phrases.notes: Still מלכים ב 3:27. The word לָאָרֶץ can also mean "to the ground," and that is what the next teaching builds on.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa says:
At that time,
the enemies of Israel went down
phrases.notes: He really means ישראל itself; the גמרא says it this way to avoid speaking badly of them.

phrases.english: to the lowest level.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַיִּסְעוּ מֵעָלָיו וַיָּשׁוּבוּ לָאָרֶץ״. אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק from step 27, now its final words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At the time of the king of מואב's sacrifice, ישראל fell to the lowest spiritual level.

steps.title: אבישג did not reach half of שרה's beauty
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר פפא reads the words 'עד מאד' in the פסוק about אבישג as 'up to very.' That means her beauty fell short of 'very,' so it did not reach even half of שרה's beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says about אבישג: 'And the young woman was very fair (עד מאד).' רבי חנינא בר פפא says: She still did not reach half of שרה's beauty. The פסוק says 'עד מאד,' meaning 'up to very,' and that does not include 'very' itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about אבישג, and רבי חנינא בר פפא explains it with a close reading of the wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עד can mean 'up to' without including the end point. So 'עד מאד' means her beauty came close to 'very' but did not reach it. The תורה calls שרה simply 'very fair' (יפה מאד), so the comparison shows that אבישג was below שרה's level.

keyTerms.meaning: Young woman. Here it refers to אבישג, who served דוד המלך in his old age.
Usually 'very much.' Here it is read as 'up to very.'

phrases.english: "And the young woman was very fair."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 1:4. This is about אבישג, who took care of דוד המלך at the end of his life.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa says:
She still did not reach
half the beauty of Sarah,
as it is written: "up to very,"
phrases.notes: He is reading עד as 'up to,' so it stops right before the word after it.

phrases.english: but "very" itself is not included.
phrases.notes: About שרה the פסוק simply says she was 'very fair' (בראשית 12:14).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אגדה from the same speaker as step 30, רבי חנינא בר פפא. It is the closing teaching of the פרק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'עד מאד' mean 'up to very' and do not include 'very.' So אבישג's beauty did not reach half of שרה's.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אחד דיני ממונות
steps.stepSummary: The traditional closing line marks the end of the chapter אחד דיני ממונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'אחד דיני ממונות.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the הדרן, the formal sign-off that closes the chapter. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן expresses a commitment to come back and learn the chapter again. The chapter is named after its opening words, אחד דיני ממונות.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the closing formula said at the end of a chapter.
Monetary cases. These words are part of the chapter's name.

steps.whatToRemember: The chapter ends with an אגדה from רבי חנינא בר פפא. He reads 'עד מאד' as 'up to very,' so אבישג fell short of שרה's beauty.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
"Both monetary cases" (the name of the chapter).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter right after its final אגדה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of פרק אחד דיני ממונות.
